articles.title: Indian-Led Team Finds UBC 63 Is Two Star Clusters After a Close Flyby
articles.excerpt: Gaia data show the cluster catalogued as one system is a 21-million-year-old cluster and a 562-million-year-old cluster that passed within 23 light-years about 6 million years ago.
articles.image_caption: The Pleiades star cluster illuminating the night sky, in a file photograph.

sources.label: The Astronomical Journal — Biswas et al.

articles.nri_angle: A Gauhati University and IIA-led team used public ESA Gaia data to revise a Milky Way catalogue entry, a model for Indian research groups competing with survey data and computing rather than telescope access.

articles.title: Jim Cramer Wants SpaceX Stock but Refuses to Buy Before Share Unlocks
articles.excerpt: Strong AI-driven earnings tempt the Mad Money host, but a $35 billion-plus spending plan and lockup expirations through mid-2027 keep him on the sidelines.
articles.image_caption: CNBC host Jim Cramer in a file photograph. Cramer says he wants SpaceX shares for his charitable trust but will not buy before share unlocks expire.
articles.nri_angle: SpaceX's AI compute buildout and its Nvidia chip orders are closely watched by Indian tech professionals and investors following the US AI infrastructure trade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Truck Simulator Rebuilds Delhi's Real Road Network for a 2027 PC Release
articles.excerpt: IronFort Studios' single-player trucking game is built from real Delhi-NCR map data — NH44 to the Delhi-Meerut Expressway — with painted trucks, dhaba stops, fatigue that builds faster in afternoon heat, and a Steam wishlist open now.
articles.image_caption: A screenshot from Indian Truck Simulator shows a painted truck on an Indian highway. The game is built from real Delhi-NCR map data and is slated for a 2027 release.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora gamers who grew up riding these highways, a Delhi-NCR built from real map data — dhabas, truck art and all — is the draw; the wishlist is open now ahead of the 2027 release and a demo.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's TPU in Orbit Answers Its First Prompt With a Haiku
articles.excerpt: Google says the Project Suncatcher prototype, launched October 1 with four TPUs aboard, generated a Gemma 4 haiku in orbit — a first test, not a working space data center.
articles.nri_angle: Orbital compute is a research test for now; for Indian-origin engineers in AI infrastructure, the signal is where Google is testing next — thermal and radiation performance, then linked satellites in 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hackers Probed Europe's Fridge Systems for 10 Days Before Attacks
articles.excerpt: Lupovis says more than 276 probing attempts preceded the November 2-3 attacks on Danfoss refrigeration controllers in nine countries — but who was behind them remains unestablished.
articles.nri_angle: The lesson travels: any remotely managed controller — in a store, warehouse, clinic or data centre — needs to be off the open internet, behind a VPN, with default passwords changed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Rental Deal in Wider Partnership Review
articles.excerpt: Bloomberg reported Microsoft declined to renew the 2023 Oracle contract and has been switching off rented capacity built on an older generation of Nvidia chips; Oracle shares fell nearly 3%.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft and Oracle are major employers of Indian and diaspora cloud and AI engineers, and a consolidation of rented AI capacity around newer hardware affects the suppliers and teams built around older-generation infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion at $1.25 Trillion Valuation, Short of Its Target

sources.label: The Inference (Financial Times and Wall Street Journal reporting)

articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora engineers, founders and investors concentrated in the US AI industry face a repricing of frontier AI capital, with OpenAI's reported round closing below its original size and valuation ambitions.

articles.title: A Hyderabad Student's Rs 68,000 Satellite Receiver Brings Weather Images to Himalayan Villages
articles.excerpt: Aagam Jain's SummitSathi pulls cloud images straight from weather satellites — no internet, no mobile signal. Three units will serve 10 villages in Himachal's Seraj valley, where networks fail in monsoon emergencies.
articles.nri_angle: A school-built, patent-filed Indian innovation aimed at disaster-prone Himalayan villages — the kind of grassroots technology story diaspora readers follow from home-state India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI-Assisted Hackers Target Indian Fintechs on Weekends, CERT-In Warns of Escalation
articles.excerpt: CERT-In has named the actor CRAFTY FALCON in a critical advisory, saying attackers use AI tools to abuse victims' own payment APIs, steal crypto wallet keys and return to firms even after they tried to fix earlier breaches.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora users who send money or invest through Indian fintech, lending and crypto apps should keep transaction alerts on and scrutinise unfamiliar small test transfers, the precursor step in this campaign.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Use Is Rising but Spending Has Stalled, Ramp Data Shows, as Anthropic Nears IPO
articles.excerpt: Token spend grew just 1.5% across August and September after a 42% jump in July, as price cuts and thriftier customers cap revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services and AI startups selling into US enterprises face the same buyer discipline Ramp documents — usage up, budgets flat.

articles.nri_angle: Many diaspora tech workers built careers in Bengaluru's IT services industry; Karnataka's push toward creative, IP-owning AI-era work signals how the jobs they left — and may return to — are changing.

articles.title: X Tells Delhi High Court an Impostor Sent Fake Takedown Notices Targeting IFF and SFLC
articles.excerpt: X said the notices seeking removal of the Internet Freedom Foundation and SFLC.in accounts were not sent by the Delhi Police, that it had not acted on them, and that it has complained to the police about the impersonation.
articles.nri_angle: The case shows how easily an official-looking takedown demand can threaten lawful speech online — a verification problem for platforms, newsrooms and diaspora-run digital-rights groups alike.

articles.title: Broadcom Sinks 9% as AI Regulation Fears Deepen Chip Rout
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker had no news of its own, but a post-midterm scare over data center limits and AI rules knocked more than 10 percent off the semiconductor index.
articles.image_caption: Broadcom headquarters. The chipmaker's shares fell 9% as AI regulation fears deepened a rout in semiconductor stocks.
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom is a core holding in many Indian American tech portfolios and retirement accounts, and its AI order book underpins jobs across the US semiconductor supply chain.

articles.excerpt: The design platform's first growth slowdown in ten years has triggered its first mass restructuring — a case study in how AI raises costs for the companies it also competes with.
articles.nri_angle: Canva is a daily tool for many diaspora creators and small businesses; its AI cost squeeze mirrors what Indian SaaS and design teams are facing on serving costs.

articles.nri_angle: Infosys is a major employer and vendor for diaspora technology professionals and US clients; added Hyderabad AI and cloud delivery capacity affects both groups.

articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm's shift from phone chips toward automotive, IoT and AI data centers matters for India's large chip-design workforce and for smartphone prices across the diaspora.

articles.excerpt: The November 2026 security bulletin patches a zero-interaction remote code execution bug and an 'SMS of Death' flaw that can crash the calling service.
articles.nri_angle: Android is the default phone platform for most users in India and much of the diaspora; whether a phone still receives monthly patches decides whether these 216 fixes, including a zero-interaction exploit, ever arrive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Dismantles XCPE Botnet Hidden in 1.3 Million Android TV Boxes
articles.excerpt: Google says Videostrong, an Android device maker, intentionally preloaded a firmware backdoor that turned its set-top boxes into a proxy and ad-fraud botnet, and it has banned the company from certified Android devices after a coordinated takedown.

sources.label: Google Cloud Blog / Google Threat Intelligence Group

articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of infected boxes were counted in the United States, and low-cost Android TV boxes bought to watch international channels are the class of device owners should check, disconnect or replace if suspect.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO Is Chance to End Deferred Stock Pay, FT Argues
articles.excerpt: The Financial Times used Anthropic's listing to argue, as opinion, that regulators should stop letting companies defer stock-based compensation costs, a practice that leaves $23.7 billion of Anthropic employee pay to be recognized only after its IPO.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-origin technology workers and investors weighing the Anthropic listing, the filing shows $23.7 billion of stock compensation still to be recognized after the IPO, a cost the adjusted profit figures add back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Makes School Search and AI Off by Default — and Schools Still Cannot Get Search Without AI

After a backlash, it clarified schools can decline Gemini and keep Search — but Search itself now comes with AI Overviews that cannot be switched off.
articles.nri_angle: Indian parents in US school districts are directly affected: whether a child school account has Search, and what AI comes with it, is now a district administrator decision, not a Google default.

articles.title: Sam Altman: Human Control Must Ultimately Constrain AI Progress
articles.excerpt: In a post on X, the OpenAI chief executive said people must never be reduced to doing what AI systems decide to reward — and that keeping humans in control should set a ceiling on how far AI advances.

articles.nri_angle: Organic photovoltaics are a field where Indian research groups and diaspora scientists are active; a clearer design rule for cutting voltage losses matters to anyone tracking where lightweight solar goes next.

articles.title: Windows 11 Gains Cloud Rebuild: Reinstall From the Cloud Even When the PC Won't Boot
articles.excerpt: The KB5127936 preview update downloads a Windows image and your drivers from Windows Update — no USB stick needed — but it wipes the system disk, so read the warning first.
articles.image_caption: A graphic shows a laptop beneath a cloud carrying the Windows logo. Cloud rebuild reinstalls Windows 11 using an image and drivers downloaded from Windows Update, even when the PC cannot start.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora tech workers and the family members who are their default IT support, a no-USB rebuild makes rescuing a parent's dead PC a phone-guided job.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Install the optional KB5127936 preview update
steps.detail: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates. The feature rolls out gradually, so it may not appear immediately.

steps.step: Back up anything stored only on the PC
steps.detail: Cloud rebuild reformats the system disk and removes all local files, accounts, apps and settings. Cloud-stored files are unaffected.
If the PC boots: Settings > System > Recovery > Rebuild PC. If it does not: in WinRE, choose Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild.
Join Ethernet or Wi-Fi, review the target build, edition and language, and confirm the data-loss warning. Keep the PC plugged in.
"Remove files" is faster; "Remove & sanitize files" is irreversible and is the right choice before selling or handing on the PC.
